name: Graph-Substrate Unification (one graph / one head / structure-tools read at it)
description: Andrew-direct via MSTR (LD-0228, IMMEDIATE/P0; brief a70daceb1). The SUBSTRATE layer beneath NFRA_COMPUNIFY: get to ONE graph, ONE marker-published HEAD, where every structure-tool (comp-blast/trace/xref/platinum) reads the Kuzu projection of THAT graph AT that head -- no agent ever checks various graphs at various states. GROUNDED current state (MSTR-verified, not assumed): the unified graph already LARGELY EXISTS (NFRA_GLOBGRPH PRD §1; Kuzu spans aws 1451/ms 5427/portal 11338, Nessie+marker-headed; NFRA_TSGRAPH folding component-level in). The fragmentation is at the TOOL layer: comp-blast/trace/xref read a separate local cache (.comp-graph/graph.json, comp-build-rebuilt TraceGraph); comp-platinum reads its own full-stack cache; comp-graph tracks them as SEPARATE vintages. So this is a RE-POINT + COMPLETE + RETIRE, NOT a graph rebuild. Four pieces: D1 complete the unified graph's coverage of what each structure-tool traverses (function-level + symbol + full-stack edges; component-level via TSGRAPH); D2 re-point the four tools onto the unified Kuzu graph at the marker head; D3 retire the local caches + comp-build's separate build (re-point THEN retire); D4 one head asserted (COMPDRIFT seam-4 generalized to every structure-tool). LOAD-BEARING RISK (CVO-owned): no-regression -- a re-pointed comp-blast/platinum MUST return the SAME answers as the pre-delta caches; mitigation = a frozen pre-delta answer fixture captured in P0, set-equality verified post-re-point per-tool.
